safety_verdicts.content: Headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated describes onset and features but does not explicitly state the headache is still present at the time of consultation.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting that the headache is ongoing at the time of the visit can reduce clarity about current symptom burden and urgency, which may affect follow-up decisions or re-triage. However, it is unlikely to directly change acute management in most headache assessments.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No mention of neck stiffness (or denial) appears in the Generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Neck stiffness is a key red-flag symptom for meningitis/subarachnoid hemorrhage workups; omission of its explicit denial weakens documentation of safety screening. This most commonly leads to extra reassessment or cautious escalation rather than direct harm when the patient actually denied it.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: No fever/fever denial is not included in the Generated facts.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Fever is another important red flag in headache evaluation (infection/meningitis) and its absence supports outpatient management. Failure to document the denial can impair downstream clinical reasoning and may prompt unnecessary urgent evaluation or repeat questioning.

safety_verdicts.content: Paracetamol taken by the patient did not relieve the headache.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not document that paracetamol was taken and did not relieve the headache.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Whether paracetamol was ineffective helps gauge severity and guides next-step therapy (NSAIDs, migraine-specific agents) and reassessment thresholds. Omitting this detail mainly affects treatment optimization and continuity rather than causing direct injury.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated does not mention denial of thoughts of self-harm.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not recording a denial of self-harm thoughts leaves an important safety assessment incomplete in the chart and could lead to inappropriate risk stratification or missed handoff information. In most settings this results in repeated assessment or additional monitoring, but it can affect psychological safety planning if relied upon.
